title: VoltPilot Redpanda telemetry-v2.raw Event
description: Event written by the Ingest service to the Redpanda topic `telemetry-v2.raw` after ENVELOPE-validating an inbound mqtt-telemetry-2.0 payload (see mqtt-telemetry-2.0.md). Consumed by the TimescaleDB-Writer's v2 listener, which explodes it into generic (entity_id, channel, value) rows in the `telemetry_v2` hypertable. Lives NEXT TO the v1 `telemetry.raw` topic (dual-consume, coexistence philosophy #2 - the v1 event contract telemetry-raw.event.schema.json is untouched). A brand-new event contract, so schema_version starts at 1.0.

x-kafka.partitioning: by tenant_id/site_id for ordered per-site processing (the v1 rule)

event_id.description: Unique id assigned by Ingest, for traceability. Idempotency downstream keys on (entity_id, channel, time), not on this id.

observed_at.description: The payload's top-level ts. An entity carrying its own ts overrides this for that entity's rows.

ingested_at.description: Time the Ingest service accepted the message; becomes received_at on every exploded row (liveness derives from arrival time, never observed_at).

seq.description: The box's per-device sequence number (mqtt-telemetry-2.0 `seq`), forwarded UNCHANGED by Ingest (UEMS AP-07 IP-5, mqtt-telemetry-2.0.md §5). ABSENT when the box sent none - absent means "not reported", never 0. A marker for gap detection (sequence_gap / sequence_reset with strom = telemetry), not part of any write key. Additive: a consumer that does not know the field ignores it (the writer's Spring ObjectMapper does).

entities.description: The validated entities block, carried through unchanged from the MQTT payload (see mqtt-telemetry-2.0.schema.json) - minus the values Ingest refused (UEMS AP-07 IP-5: a bad channel, an entity without readable ts/channels, or an implausible measurement time drops only those values; each refusal lands as a datenannahme event on events.raw).
